title: Enterprise intake: operational-risk & usage-pattern scoring for hosted API feature requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Build an operational-risk and usage-pattern scoring rubric for incoming Hosted API feature requests from enterprise customers (chat, streaming, function/tool-calls, structured outputs). The rubric will surface requests that require: (a) Dedicated/Private engagement, (b) security/compliance review, (c) engineering capacity planning, or (d) can be handled self-serve. Goals: reduce intake cycle time, ensure SLA-aligned prioritization, and make routing decisions reproducible and auditable.
scoring_summary: We propose a 100-point composite score comprised of four pillars: Customer Risk (30), Usage Predictability & Volume (25), Technical Impact (25), Compliance & Data Sensitivity (20). Thresholds map to rails: 0-34 = Self-Serve backlog; 35-64 = Design Consult (PM + Solutions Eng); 65-84 = Dedicated Implementation (Dedicated/Private sales); 85-100 = Escalate to Enterprise Success + Security. Score factors include expected TPS/requests per minute, peak concurrency, KV-cache needs, streaming/real-time requirements, function-calling surface area, structured output validation rules, data residency, and legal/compliance flags.
deliverables: automated scoring lambda + mapping rules (pooled service)
Triage dashboard in Console for PM/SE visibility
acceptance_criteria: Scoring prototype calculates a deterministic score for 20 historical enterprise requests (sample) and matches manual PM prioritization in >= 80% of cases
Intake form contains explicit fields required to compute each pillar (customer size, expected qps, streaming flag, PII flag, required SLO)
Routing outputs (self-serve/design-consult/dedicated/escalate) are surfaced as structured fields in intake webhook
Documentation and playbook published in Confluence and linked from Console intake UI
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: KPI for this ticket is to reduce time-to-first-response on enterprise feature requests from 5 business days to 48 hours by automating basic triage. Initial hypothesis: usage pattern + compliance flags explain most prioritization variance.

2026-03-11 Marco Li (Assignee): Worked with Eng infra to list telemetry inputs we can use for usage prediction (token distribution, historical qps, latency percentiles). ENG owners: @Ravi Shah for runtime signals, @Sofia Kim for quota/usage datasets.

2026-03-12 Design review: Recommended a compact intake form that avoids free-text where possible; add structured enums for 'streaming type' (none / server-stream / client-stream / bidi) and 'tool-calling complexity' (simple / multi-step / external-auth). Design lead: Lena Ortiz.

2026-03-12 Security: Security review required. Need to add explicit 'data residency' and 'PII indicator' fields to intake. Security contact: Omar Hassan. Action: schedule 30-min sync to validate thresholds that trigger mandatory security engagement.

2026-03-13 Product note: Mapped initial weightings and ran scoring on 25 past intake items from last 12 months. Results: 9 items moved from 'manual review' to 'self-serve', 6 were correctly escalated to Dedicated, 10 flagged for security review. Spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-redwood/PM-61702-scoring-prototype

2026-03-13 Eng feedback (Ravi Shah): For streaming-heavy workloads we need to capture expected average and max sequence length (affects KV cache sizing). Suggested adding 'avg_seq_len' as optional numeric input in intake form.

2026-03-14 PM decision: Lock fields for MVP intake: customer_tier, expected_qps_peak, expected_qps_avg, streaming_flag, streaming_type, function_calls_per_request, structured_output_schema_present (yes/no), pii_flag, data_residency_region, requested_slo_ms. Next: wire webhook spec and prototype scoring lambda. Owner: Marco Li.

2026-03-14 Next steps: 1) Marco to publish intake form draft and webhook spec (due 2026-03-16). 2) Eng to prototype scoring lambda and run historical batch (Ravi & Sofia, due 2026-03-20). 3) Security sync (Omar) scheduled for 2026-03-16. 4) Create Console triage dashboard ticket (PM-61721).
notes: We should avoid overfitting weights to past enterprise tickets that were handled inconsistently. Score should be explainable: each pillar must return a short rationale string (MVP maps to canned rationales). Long-term goal: feed intake decisions to 'routes' used by sales and solutions engineering to automate discovery meetings and contract recommendations.
business_value_summary: Faster, reproducible routing of enterprise feature requests reduces friction for high-value customers and lets Eng/SE focus on work with material infrastructure or compliance impact. Also provides early signals for Dedicated/private demand forecasting.
timebox: 6 weeks to MVP: intake form + scoring lambda + dashboard + playbook
